name: Sun acupuncture for CP/CPPS
question: Does acupuncture improve symptoms more than sham acupuncture in men with moderate to severe chronic prostatitis/chronic pelvic pain syndrome?

design.population: 440 men with moderate to severe chronic prostatitis/chronic pelvic pain syndrome at ten tertiary hospitals in China.
design.locator: PubMed abstract, Design, Setting, Participants, Results

verdictNote: Responder differences were significant at both prespecified time points.
takeaway: In men with moderate to severe chronic prostatitis/chronic pelvic pain syndrome, 20 acupuncture sessions over 8 weeks produced more NIH-CPSI responders than sham acupuncture at both week 8 and week 32.

reports.label: Primary report
reports.citation: Sun Y, Liu Y, Liu B, et al. "Efficacy of Acupuncture for Chronic Prostatitis/Chronic Pelvic Pain Syndrome: A Randomized Trial." *Ann Intern Med.* 2021;174(10):1357-1366. doi:10.7326/M21-1814
reports.followUp: 8-week treatment; assessment at weeks 8 and 32 (24 weeks after treatment)

results.measure: Week-8 proportion with at least a 6-point NIH-CPSI reduction; adjusted risk difference in percentage points
results.note: Sustained efficacy required statistical significance at both weeks 8 and 32; response percentages and effect are reported estimates.

results.measure: Week-32 proportion with at least a 6-point NIH-CPSI reduction; adjusted risk difference in percentage points
results.note: Week 32 was 24 weeks after treatment ended; response percentages and effect are reported estimates.

harms.label: Reported adverse events
harms.note: The abstract reports events, without event types or severity distribution.

harms.label: Serious adverse events
harms.note: No serious adverse events were reported.
